name: Skye Bridge
facts: Skye Bridge, a single‑span concrete arch 500 metres long, opened on 16 October 1995 after £27 million of PFI‑funded construction, replacing a ferry that once carried 300,000 vehicles a year.
The bridge sparked a decade‑long toll battle; by 2004 a round‑trip cost £11.40, and £33.3 million had been collected before Scottish ministers finally bought it and abolished tolls.
Its two caissons were cast as hollow cylinders in Kishorn Dry Dock, floated across Loch Alsh, then sunk onto the loch bed—an engineering feat that linked Skye to mainland Scotland.
